The primary text is Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (MML) — [free PDF](https://mml-book.github.io/). Boyd & Vandenberghe, MacKay, and Solomon provide the main supplementary readings.

## Course format

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| Credits | 3-1-0-4 |
| Instructor | Prof. Nipun Batra, IIT Gandhinagar |
| Meetings | 26 lectures and 13 tutorials; 80 minutes each |
| Tutorial format | Pen-and-paper worksheet followed by a computational notebook |
| Primary text | Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* |

**Prerequisites:** ES 113 (Data Centric Computing) and ES 114 (Probability, Statistics & Data Visualisation). We assume Python/NumPy and basic discrete probability. We do **not** assume any machine learning.

**Assessment structure:** quizzes at module boundaries (best n−1), a mid-semester examination after Module 3, a cumulative end-semester examination, and three take-home assignments (micrograd, CVXPY, and compression plus a language model). Tutorials are formative.

## Learning outcomes

By the end of the course, students should be able to:

1. diagnose common floating-point failures and choose numerically stable forms of elementary computations;
2. use vector, matrix, eigenvalue, SVD, and PCA calculations to describe data and linear maps;
3. compute gradients, Jacobians, and Hessians, and implement forward- and reverse-mode automatic differentiation on small graphs;
4. work with continuous and multivariate distributions and derive MLE and MAP estimators in standard models;
5. formulate and solve unconstrained, equality-constrained, and inequality-constrained optimization problems, including LPs and QPs;
6. compute entropy, cross-entropy, KL divergence, and expected code length; and
7. fit, evaluate, and sample from a finite-state Markov or n-gram sequence model.

## Alignment with the approved proposal

The sequence covers numerical representation, linear algebra, multivariate calculus and automatic differentiation, probabilistic modelling and estimation, continuous and constrained optimization, information-theoretic foundations, and sequential models. Theory and programming are paired throughout the course.
